title: Troye Sivan Enjoys ‘Best’ Start on ARIA Chart
summary: Olivia Dean is still feeling the love from her Australian arena tour, as "The Art Of Loving" holds at No. 1 on the ARIA Albums Chart.
contentText:
Olivia Dean is still the best , certainly with respect to Australia’s official albums tally. But Troye Sivan isn’t far behind.

Dean’s The Art Of Loving (via Universal) retains top spot on the ARIA Albums Chart , while Sivan’s fourth studio album, She’s The Best (EMI), opens its account at No. 2. An eight-time ARIA Award winner, Sivan peaked out at No. 6 with 2015’s Blue Neighbourhood , No. 3 in 2018 with Bloom and enjoyed a week at No. 1 with 2023’s Something To Give Each Other .

Dean is still feeling the love from her Australian arena tour, which wrapped up this week and sends her sophomore LP back to No. 1 on the ARIA Chart for a 15th non-consecutive cycle. On the singles tally, she has no less than six titles in the top 40.

Tame Impala is also on the road in Australia, and enjoying a lift on the ARIA Albums Chart as 2025’s Deadbeat (Columbia/Sony) rises 47-5. Kevin Parker and Co. will play Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena tonight and Monday (Oct. 19), followed by three shows at Sydney’s Afterpay Arena and a pair of concerts at RAC Arena in his hometown, Perth. Frontier Touring, Chugg Entertainment and Laneway Presents are promoting the 12-date national Deadbeat tour .

Geese frontman Cameron Winter bags a top 10 entry on the ARIA Chart, published late Friday, Oct. 16, with Live At Carnegie Hall (PIAS/Inertia), at No. 8, while Chase & Status are close behind with Generic Everything (Warner) at No. 9. That’s easily a career-best chart position for the British drum ‘n’ bass act, which has released seven albums for a previous best of No. 38 for 2013’s Brand New Machine .

U.S. singer and songwriter Remi Wolf ( Mud at No. 20 via Island/Universal), British electro-pop veterans Pet Shop Boys ( A man from the Future at No. 22 via Parlophone/Warner), Sydney alt-pop artist Darcy Lane ( Vampires & Liars at No. 32), Western Australian rock act Grub ( Grub at No. 36 via MGM), and international girl group Katseye ( Wild at No. 44 via Interscope/Universal) enjoy top 40 berths.

Over on the ARIA Singles Chart , Taylor Swift ’s “Patient Zero” (Republic/Universal) improves 2-1, for a second non-consecutive week at No. 1. The top debut belongs to Welsh singer Jamie Miller, whose “Babydoll” (Universal) appears at No. 35.
